reframing_when: The question keeps producing cleaner versions of the same answer because hidden assumptions in the question's frame remain unchallenged — the blockage is conceptual, not effort-based.
The question is locked into a single disciplinary lens when the problem lives at the intersection of multiple fields — the 'if all you have is a hammer' pattern is active.
The question asks 'how do we fix X?' when the more productive question is 'How Might We think about X differently?' — divergence is needed before convergence.
The question assumes the current reality is the only possible frame when a thought experiment ('what would it look like if...?') would open a fundamentally different option space.
reframing_move: Break the frame by asking the question from outside its own discipline: instead of refining the question within its current frame, apply SCAMPER (Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Minimize, Put to another use, Eliminate, Reverse) or ask 'what would need to be true for a completely different approach to work?' — the Airbnb reframe that changed the venture capital conversation.
curation_note: Lateral thinking is a meta-reframing model — its entire purpose is generating questions that the current frame cannot produce. The source explicitly describes HMW (How Might We) as a question-generation framework that must be separated from solution generation. The Airbnb VC example is a canonical case of question-level reframing changing a decision.

reframing_when.note: All four activations grounded: stale options from unchallenged assumptions (source explicit), hammer/nail pattern (Maslow's hammer), divergence before convergence (HMW methodology), thought experiments as frame-breakers (workplace example).

frame_patterns_challenged.note: Binary collapse: lateral thinking opens the option space beyond A/B. Option space collapse: divergent thinking widens before narrowing. Habitual frame: the multi-disciplinary lens breaks professional frame distortion.
